svg.text: WHAT THE MODEL SAYS
WHAT IT DRAWS
The filter is not choosing between your two sensors. Every step it decides how far to
move its current belief towards the new measurement, and that distance is a ratio of two
uncertainties.
It tracks how wrong it expects to be. Alongside the position estimate the filter carries
a covariance, P, which is its own claim about how unsure it is. Prediction steps the
state forward with the odometry and adds process noise Q, so P grows: every second
without a fix, the filter knows less. The measurement arrives with its own noise, R. In
the scalar case the gain is K = P-/(P- + R), model uncertainty over total uncertainty.
If the prediction is ten times less certain than the fix, K is near 1 and the estimate
jumps most of the way to the GPS. If the fix is the noisy one, K is near 0 and the
estimate barely moves. Nothing in there asks which sensor is better in general, only
which is less sure right now.
What gets corrected is the disagreement. The correction is K times the innovation, the
difference between the fix and what the model expected. That is why the two failure
modes you describe cancel: GPS jitter is zero-mean, so repeated small corrections
average out rather than accumulating, while odometry drift is a steady bias that the
innovation sees as a growing disagreement and keeps pulling back. Each sensor covers the
other's weakness, and the gain is what decides the balance moment by moment.
The lurch is Q being wrong, not the filter. Q is a claim about how far the motion model
can be off in one step. Wheel slip violates it: the odometry reports travel that did not
happen, and the error is far larger than Q admits. The filter has no way to know. It
still believes its prediction is good, so P- stays small, K stays small, the GPS fix is
discounted as noise, and the estimate follows a prediction that is simply wrong. It
recovers, but slowly, because it has to accumulate enough innovation to overcome its own
confidence.
The fix is not a larger Q everywhere, which throws away the odometry's real precision
between slips. It is to notice the slip and inflate Q for those steps, from a
wheel-encoder disagreement, an IMU, or a current spike. Failing that, gate on the
innovation itself: if it is much larger than the square root of P- + R, the filter's own
numbers say something it believes cannot be true, and that is the moment to stop
trusting the model.
